newsitem.title: USA: Gen'l aviation says wrongly excluded from US panel.
newsitem.headline: Gen'l aviation says wrongly excluded from US panel.

text.p: A helicopter trade group said on Thursday that the general aviation industry has been wrongly excluded from representation on a new civil aviation review commission and the industry may take legal action.
Frank Jensen, president of the Helicopter Association International, said the general aviation industry had formed a coalition to protest the makeup of the National Civil Aviation Review Commission.

He said the group, representing nearly all the 200,000 general aviation aircraft users, would first try to negotiate to win a voice on the panel, but he would not rule out taking legal action to get representation.
Asked about such action, Jensen said, "We think it really is a serious issue and we will take whatever action we think is necessary."

The commission was created by Congress to assess the nation's future aviation needs, including how to finance the Federal Aviation Administration. Congress named eight members to the panel and the Transportation Department named 13.

Jensen said the law creating the panel called for it to represent a balanced view of the issues important to the entire aviation industry, and by excluding general aviation, the panel was violating the very law that established it.

He said "the recent appointments filling the 21-member panel reflect air carriers and airports only" and while they are experts in their areas, "not one has substantial experience in General Aviation."
Members of the coalition fighting the makeup of the panel, Jensen said, include the General Aviation Manufacturers Association and the Aircraft Owners and Pilots Association.

A major point of dispute between the general aviation industry and the major airlines is how to apportion FAA financing needs fairly between assessments on the major airlines, start-up airlines, and the operators of the smaller planes of the general aviation industry.
There was no immediate comment on the make up of the panel from the Transportation Department.
Aides to House of Representatives Minority leader Richard Gephardt, a Missouri Democrat, said the Congressmen had only two selections, but tried to make them representative of all facets of aviation.

There was no immediate comment from other Congressional leaders who made selections. They are Republican House Speaker Newt Gingrich of Georgia, Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott, a Mississippi Republican, and Senate Minority Leader Thomas Daschle, a South Dakota Democrat.
